Ulla Dam-Schmidt is a specialized nurse (*Sygeplejerske med klinisk specialfunktion*) holding a Master's degree (MKS, SD) and working at Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg Hospital [^src1] [^src2]. She plays a pivotal leadership role in Denmark's national quality improvement efforts for cardiovascular health, specifically concerning the treatment and management of atrial fibrillation. 

She serves in the top leadership of the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK). In the 2023 annual report, she is listed alongside medical doctors Lars Frost and Albert Marni Joensen as part of the database's joint chairmanship, representing the crucial nursing perspective within the [[afdk-styregruppe|Styregruppen for AFDK]] [^src1]. By the 2024 annual report, she is explicitly named as the primary chairperson (*Forperson*) for the database [^src3] and continues her active membership in the steering group [^src4]. 

Her involvement ensures that patient pathways, structured patient education, and interdisciplinary collaboration are integrated into the clinical recommendations and quality metrics of the [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] initiative [^src4]. The AFDK reports, published under the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), rely on multidisciplinary leadership to bridge hospital-centered and population-based quality measurements across Denmark's healthcare clusters [^src3] [^src4]. Through her work, Dam-Schmidt helps guide national strategies for treating a frequent and potentially serious chronic heart condition, emphasizing evidence-based and patient-centered care [^src4].
